papers.title: Multi-parametric spectral modeling disentangles synaptic kinetics and neural excitability from non-invasive electrophysiological recordings
papers.abstract: Spectral modeling of electrophysiological recordings enables non-invasive characterization of neural excitability. However, current approaches rely on a single spectral index, limiting insight into the multiple biophysical processes underlying excitation-inhibition balance. Here, we introduce a biologically informed, multi-parametric spectral analysis that disentangles neural excitability and synaptic kinetics from recordings. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate that this approach captures signatures of hyperexcitability and glutamate reuptake dysfunction characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.

ai.reason: Directly provides an interpretable, biologically informed spectral decomposition method for non-invasive electrophysiology, highly relevant to the researcher's spectral modeling and EEG analysis interests.

papers.title: Slow-wave sleep selectively amplifies network signatures of the presumed epileptogenic zone in focal epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Slow-wave sleep increases interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and seizures in focal epilepsy, but how sleep stages reshape epileptogenic tissue remains unclear. We assessed whether sleep stages selectively modulate network properties of the presumed epileptogenic zone (pEZ) relative to irritative (IZ) and non-involved (NIZ) zones. We studied 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing pre-surgical intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG). IED-free resting-state epochs spanned four vigilance stages: wakefulness, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep stages 2 and 3, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Spectral power, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic indices, and the 1/f exponent were quantified across seven frequency bands. Sleep stage and zone interactions were tested using permutation testing. pEZ electrodes were classified using elastic net logistic regression with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. NREM3 selectively amplified within-pEZ gamma-band synchrony beyond surrounding zones (pEZ-NIZ: d=1.204, P=0.027). pEZ local efficiency and betweenness centrality rose in beta1 and gamma bands versus wakefulness. The aperiodic exponent steepened within the IZ versus NIZ during NREM3 and NREM2 (d =1.452 and 0.87, P < 0.001 and P=0.015). A three-feature classifier (NREM3 aperiodic exponent, beta2 connectivity, gamma local efficiency) localised the pEZ without ictal recordings (median AUC 0.859 pEZ vs. non-pEZ). Slow-wave sleep selectively unmasks pEZ network properties via amplified power, synchrony and hub topology. NREM3-derived multimodal features may complement conventional pre-surgical biomarkers. Prospective validation in larger cohorts is needed to determine whether these markers improve surgical planning and outcome prediction.

ai.reason: Directly uses iEEG spectral power, connectivity, 1/f exponent, and cross-validated classification across vigilance states, highly transferable to sleep staging and state-dependent network analysis.
ai.summary: In 22 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing intracranial EEG, NREM3 slow-wave sleep selectively amplified within-pEZ gamma-band synchrony and hub topology versus surrounding zones, and a three-feature NREM3 classifier localised the presumed epileptogenic zone without ictal recordings (median AUC 0.859).

papers.title: Tensor decomposition reveals discrete cortical reorganization under graded propofol anesthesia.
papers.abstract: Although propofol-induced anesthesia is known to suppress consciousness by promoting low-frequency frontal oscillations through thalamocortical circuits, a comprehensive understanding of its whole-brain coupling feature set remains elusive. Specifically, the global reorganization of nonlinear cross-frequency coupling remains poorly characterized due to analytical limitations. We analyzed 64-channel EEG data from 17 participants across five states (awake and target propofol concentrations of 1, 2, 3, and 4 mcg/ml, defined as States 1 to 5). After computing time-frequency representation (TFR) and bicoherence, Parallel Factor Analysis (PARAFAC) was used to extract unbiased spatio-spectral components from both linear and nonlinear measures. PARAFAC decomposition isolated distinct linear and nonlinear neurodynamic components driving the anesthetic transition. While linear spectral features and signal complexity transitioned in a gradual, monotonic manner. PARAFAC tensor decomposition of high-dimensional whole-brain bicoherence identified two robust, intrinsically decoupled nonlinear components with distinct spatial-spectral profiles. Model comparison demonstrated that frontal slow-wave self-coupling (Component 1) undergoes a discrete, stepwise state-space reconfiguration during loss of consciousness, whereas posterior alpha coupling (Component 2) exhibits a smooth, continuous decay with propofol titration. Phase-space kinetic trajectories confirmed a highly directed transition at unconsciousness onset, followed by confined local oscillations during deep anesthesia. This multi-dimensional decomposition framework captures discrete versus continuous neural dynamics, providing objective, state-sensitive biomarkers for precisely monitoring anesthesia depth and cortical state transitions.

papers.title: Longitudinal changes in resting-state EEG eyes-closed/open delta differentiation during an Antarctic expedition.
papers.abstract: Antarctic polar night brings extreme light deprivation, prolonged isolation and severe circadian disruption, yet longitudinal resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) signatures reflecting neurophysiological alterations in this harsh environment remain poorly characterized. In this exploratory longitudinal research, resting-state EEG recordings with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) were acquired from 16 Antarctic expeditioners at four mission stages: pre-departure, pre-polar-night, early post-polar-night, and austral summer. Linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate correction were applied to analyze delta eyes-closed/open differentiation (the EC-EO delta log-power difference), delta sub-bands, aperiodic spectral features, entropy, EEG microstates and delta-band functional connectivity. The delta EC-EO difference exhibited consistent, progressively negative shifts in parietal, frontal, whole-brain and occipital regions across the expedition timeline, with the most pronounced shifts observed in recordings obtained during and after the polar-night period; this effect spanned all slow, mid and fast delta sub-bands. Secondary mild temporal variations were observed in aperiodic spectral metrics, occipital sample entropy and global delta connectivity, whereas EEG microstates displayed no significant longitudinal alterations. Collectively, the delta EC-EO difference emerges as a candidate EEG index of resting-state condition differentiation in the low-frequency range, pending validation in larger studies with synchronized behavioral, physiological, and environmental measures.

ai.summary: Longitudinally tracked resting-state eyes-open/eyes-closed EEG in 16 Antarctic expeditioners across four mission stages and found progressively negative shifts in the delta EC-EO difference, most pronounced during and after polar night, with only mild changes in aperiodic metrics, entropy, connectivity, and no microstate alterations.

papers.title: The ovarian cycle and estradiol modulate cortical network state and auditory entrainment in mice and women
papers.abstract: The human brain is remarkably dynamic, continuously adapting to internal and external signals across rapid and protracted timescales. While both male and female brains are influenced by sex hormones to drive adaptive behavioural and physiological changes, the ovarian cycle in female mammals represents a conserved naturalistic model to understand how hormones such as estradiol (E2) alter cellular and network states to shape brain function. To understand whether and how the ovarian cycle influences sensory cortical processing, we investigated cortical network activity at rest and upon auditory stimulation across the ovarian cycle in mice and human subjects. We recorded EEG activity in men and women and intracortical local field potentials in male and female mice. Female participants were tested during two phases of their ovarian cycle characterized by low E2 levels (early follicular phase in women; late estrus in mice) and high E2 levels (late follicular phase in women; proestrus in mice). Across species, high endogenous or exogenous estradiol was associated with a steeper aperiodic power spectral slope, indicating decreased excitatory/inhibitory drive and attenuated auditory entrainment following a 40Hz stimulation. At the single-cell level, high E2 selectively increased the baseline and sustained 40-Hz firing of putative fast-spiking interneurons while reducing their temporal coherence during both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity, suggesting that E2 enhances inhibitory tone, while disrupting the temporal coordination of inhibitory networks. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that estradiol dynamically modulates cortical network states and auditory responsiveness. This underscores the necessity of investigating hormone-brain coupling as an evolutionarily conserved model essential for yielding translational insights into sex-specific neurobiology.

papers.title: A Humanized Mouse Model of DRPLA Recapitulates Epilepsy and Demonstrates Antisense Oligonucleotide-Mediated Disease Modification
papers.abstract: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA) is an ultra-rare progressive myoclonus epilepsy caused by a glutamine-coding CAG repeat expansion in atrophin-1 (ATN1). Mutant ATN1 (mATN1) expression results in symptoms that inversely correlate to CAG-expansion size: young-onset cases have the most CAG repeats and developmental delay, high-frequency treatment-resistant seizures, and early mortality. We sought to characterize the seizure susceptibility of a fully humanized ATN1 mouse expressing human mATN1 with 112 CAG repeats to then assess therapeutic antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) intervention on seizure-related outcomes. Atn1Q112/+ or wild-type (WT) mice were treated with investigational ASO targeting human, CAG-expanded, ATN1 or saline (P2 and then again at 4 weeks-old) before acute seizure testing, ataxia profiling, and chronic in vivo video-EEG recording for spontaneous seizures up to 8 weeks-old. Saline-treated Atn1Q112/+ mice were more seizure prone with early death. However, ASO administration to Atn1Q112/+ mice normalized seizure threshold, decreased ataxia, and protected against early death. Atn1Q112/+ mice exhibited spontaneous behavioral seizures recorded over 2 weeks, which were absent in ASO-treated Atn1Q112/+ and WT mice, with a specific mATN1 expression-driven decrease in delta and theta EEG frequencies. Atn1Q112/+ mice are highly seizure prone, validating this model for DRPLA epilepsy. ATN1 represents a novel epilepsy-related risk factor for therapeutic investigation.

ai.summary: Characterized seizure susceptibility in a fully humanized Atn1Q112/+ DRPLA mouse model and tested an antisense oligonucleotide targeting CAG-expanded ATN1. Saline-treated mutants showed increased seizure propensity and early death, while ASO treatment normalized seizure threshold, reduced ataxia, prevented spontaneous behavioral seizures, and protected against early death.

papers.title: Feasibility of unattended in-home polysomnography in trauma-exposed Veterans with chronic nightmares.
papers.abstract: This study examined the feasibility and acceptability of unattended home polysomnography (hPSG) in trauma-exposed U.S. Veterans with chronic nightmares (N = 47). Of the scheduled studies, 41 (87.2%) were completed. Twenty-four (58.5%) tests were successful based on all pre-specified criteria. Twenty-nine (71%) had ≥4 hours of interpretable EEG. No baseline differences were found between Veterans with and without successful hPSGs. Regarding acceptability, sleep quality was rated significantly worse on the night with hPSG compared to a night without. This study observed that unattended hPSG is partially feasible and acceptable in a group of trauma-exposed Veterans; however, failure was common. Characteristics of trauma-exposed samples, such as increased sweating and sleep movements, may have contributed to these results. Tools designed to be applied independently and to endure these factors should be considered.

papers.title: A sliding window and Fourier decomposition method based 1D-CNN framework for motor imagery EEG classification.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signal classification is fundamental requirement for effective motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. However, current MI classification methods often depend on handcrafted spatial filtering or complex time-frequency transformations that increase computational complexity. To mitigate this limitation, we propose a unified architecture that integrates a sliding window (SW), a Fourier decomposition method (FDM), and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) for MI-EEG classification. The raw EEG data were segmented using the SW approach to augment the data and extract more temporal feature patterns from each trial. The segmented signal, containing time-domain features, was subsequently processed using a band-pass filter and FDM to extract frequency-based features. Here, FDM decomposes the signal into eight orthogonal Fourier Intrinsic Band Functions (FIBFs). A 1D-CNN architecture was employed to learn representations from the decomposed EEG signals. The proposed framework was evaluated on the BCI Competition III Dataset IVa (BCIC III IVa) and BCI Competition IV-2a (BCIC IV 2a) datasets. Our method achieved accuracies of 79.14% and 93.67% on the BCIC IV 2a and BCIC III IVa datasets, respectively, under the subject-dependent evaluation protocol. To evaluate cross-subject generalization, the proposed framework was validated using the Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) protocol, achieving average classification accuracies of 76.49% on the BCIC III Dataset IVa and 55.50% on the BCIC IV 2a dataset. Furthermore, deployment on the NVIDIA Jetson Nano demonstrated complete pipeline latencies of 58.119 ms/trial and 85.055 ms/trial, corresponding to throughputs of 17.21 and 11.76 trials/s for the BCIC III IVa and BCIC IV 2a datasets, respectively. The results show the strong potential of the developed MI-EEG classification method to assist subjects with motor ailments.

ai.reason: CPU-friendly 1D-CNN with spectral decomposition is a moderately transferable lightweight classification pipeline, though motor-imagery-specific and lacks normalization/calibration components.
ai.summary: Proposed a sliding-window, Fourier decomposition method, and 1D-CNN pipeline for motor imagery EEG classification, evaluated on BCI Competition III Dataset IVa and IV-2a. Achieved subject-dependent accuracies of 79.14% and 93.67%, LOSO accuracies of 76.49% and 55.50%, and demonstrated Jetson Nano deployment latencies of 58–85 ms/trial.

papers.title: TCANet: a temporal convolutional attention network for EEG-based cognitive load assessment in simulated flight tasks.
papers.abstract: Effective cognitive load assessment facilitates optimized task allocation and plays a critical role in evaluating human performance in domains such as flight safety monitoring and human-computer interaction. Electroencephalography (EEG) has been extensively employed in cognitive load research owing to its high temporal resolution, non-invasiveness, and accessibility. However, EEG signals exhibit substantial variability across individuals and task conditions, making it challenging to extract stable and discriminative features related to cognitive load. Accordingly, we propose TCANet, a Temporal Convolutional Attention Network designed to learn discriminative EEG representations for cognitive load classification in simulated flight tasks. The proposed network integrates multi-branch temporal convolutions, dilated convolutions, and attention mechanisms to model temporal, spatial, and channel-wise EEG information while reducing redundant feature responses. We designed an EEG-based cognitive load classification paradigm involving two pilot-simulated flight scenarios. A total of 20 participants were recruited, with 15 participants completing the turning task and 5 participants completing the landing task. TCANet achieved average classification accuracies of 90.15% and 81.52% on the turning-task and landing-task datasets, respectively. The turning-task dataset served as the primary evaluation dataset, whereas the landing-task dataset provided a supplementary evaluation under a different simulated flight task. Statistical analyses of frequency-band power indicated task-condition-related variations in EEG spectral activity. Neurophysiological variations, particularly in the Theta and Alpha bands, and feature representation analyses further provided interpretable evidence regarding cognitive-load-related EEG patterns and the discriminative representations learned by TCANet.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Changes in Emotional Recognition: A Signal Processing Approach Using Wavelet Features.
papers.abstract: motion recognition using electroencephalography (EEG) has gained significant attention in the fields of affective computing and human-computer interaction due to its ability to capture real-time neural responses. EEG signal variations associated with emotional states can be analysed using wavelet-based signal processing within the arousal-valence framework. This study aims to analyse EEG signal variations associated with emotional states using a wavelet-based signal processing approach within the arousal-valence framework. A prospective observational study was conducted on 48 healthy participants. Emotional states were induced using image, video and music stimuli categorised under the arousal-valence model. EEG signals were recorded using the standard 10-20 electrode placement system. The acquired signals were pre-processed and analysed using discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to extract time-frequency features, including energy and entropy. Statistical analysis was performed to evaluate hemispheric differences and gender-based variations. Differences in EEG activity were observed between the left and right hemispheres across multiple emotional states (p < .05). Video and music stimuli produced stronger and more distinguishable EEG responses compared to image-based stimuli. Negative emotions demonstrated higher discriminative patterns than positive emotions. Gender-based variations were also observed in EEG responses. Wavelet-based EEG feature analysis provides meaningful and discriminative information for emotion recognition and may provide a robust feature set for future machine learning-based emotion recognition systems. Further studies incorporating classification algorithms and larger data sets are required to validate their predictive performance.

ai.summary: Analyzed EEG signal variations during emotion recognition using discrete wavelet transform features (energy and entropy) within an arousal-valence framework in 48 healthy participants. Found hemispheric differences across emotional states (p < .05), stronger discriminative EEG responses to video and music than images, and gender-based variations.

papers.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
papers.abstract: Our primary aim is to develop an automated feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of EEG recordings acquired from English-speaking and Turkish-speaking participant cohorts. Drawing inspiration from a quantum tunnel pattern called QTPat, we introduced a novel approach of dynamically generating directed graphs to extract textural features. For our experiments, we utilized an EEG dataset containing 1652 English sentence-EEG pairs and 1600 Turkish sentence-EEG pairs. These signals were recorded from 20 English-speaking and 20 Turkish subjects who were presented with standardized sentences in their respective native languages. During the experiments, the participants were instructed to carefully contemplate each sentence while wearing a mobile brain cap system that acquired 14-channel EEG signals. Our preprocessing pipeline involved subjecting the EEG signals to multiple filtered wavelet packet decompositions, using both 6 Daubechies and 6 symlet wavelet filters. Subsequently, we extracted textural and statistical features employing the QTPat model, along with 20 statistical moments. To enhance discriminative power, we applied neighborhood component analysis and the Chi2-function to select the most relevant features. The k-nearest neighbor classifier was then employed to calculate predictive vectors. To further refine the results, we introduced an iterative hard majority voting scheme, generating additional voted vectors. Finally, we utilized a greedy algorithm to select the best-channel-wise and overall model results. Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO CV), the proposed framework achieved 96.37% classification accuracy using four selected EEG channels. These findings demonstrate that the QTPat-based architecture can discriminate the two language-associated EEG cohorts under subject-independent evaluation. However, because language and participant population are coupled in the available dataset, the present results should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding. Further studies using within-subject bilingual experimental designs are required to determine whether the identified EEG patterns specifically reflect language-related neural processing.

ai.reason: Feature-engineering pipeline with wavelet-packet decomposition and subject-independent classification is relevant to interpretable feature extraction, but the quantum-pattern novelty is idiosyncratic.
ai.summary: Introduced a QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent EEG classification of English- and Turkish-associated signals, achieving 96.37% accuracy with four channels using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The authors note that the results are not definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding due to confounding between language and participant population.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo for Bayesian spectral analysis.
papers.abstract: Bayesian spectral deconvolution provides a data-driven framework for mathematical model selection and parameter estimation from spectral data. Although highly versatile, its computational cost grows with the number of model parameters, data points, and candidate models, often rendering practical applications infeasible. We propose a GPU-accelerated approach in which a sequential Monte Carlo sampler (SMCS) is executed in parallel on a GPU to perform Bayesian model selection for the number of spectral peaks and Bayesian estimation of peak-function parameters. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the GPU-parallelized SMCS reaches the free-energy accuracy of an optimized CPU-parallelized replica exchange Monte Carlo (REMC) baseline up to approximately 37× faster-with smaller gains, down to near parity, in the least favorable settings-and is faster than GPU-parallelized REMC in many of the tested cases. The method is validated on artificial data designed to emulate x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and x-ray diffraction measurements, as well as on real experimental spectra. As measurement techniques such as microscopic spectroscopy and in situ methods continue to drive rapid growth in the volume of spectral data, the proposed approach offers a practical computational foundation for advanced analysis of each individual dataset.

ai.reason: Addresses spectral deconvolution and model selection, transferable to spectral analysis, but focused on spectroscopy with GPU-heavy Monte Carlo rather than neural time-series.
ai.summary: Proposed a GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo sampler for parallel Bayesian spectral deconvolution and model selection, reaching free-energy accuracy comparable to optimized CPU replica exchange Monte Carlo up to approximately 37x faster, validated on simulated XPS/XRD-like data and real spectra.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted categorization of interictal abnormalities in adult long-term electroencephalographic monitoring: Comparable diagnostic accuracy with marked efficiency gain.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) classifies routine electroencephalograms (EEGs) with expert-level accuracy, but interpretation of long-term EEG monitoring (LTM) remains reliant on time-intensive visual review. We evaluated whether autoSCORE, a clinically approved implementation of SCORE-AI integrated into an EEG reader, achieves expert-level diagnostic accuracy for LTM interpretation and whether expert-supervised use reduces review time versus conventional analysis. A fixed-and-frozen AI model was tested on an independent single-center dataset of 78 adult patient LTM recordings (52 normal, 26 abnormal), with epilepsy monitoring unit discharge diagnosis as the external reference standard. The AI model was benchmarked against two expert panels (three readers each); Panel 1 reviewed autoSCORE EEG detections (hybrid approach), and Panel 2 interpreted full recordings (conventional approach). Diagnostic accuracy and time to diagnostic decision were assessed for fully automated, hybrid, and conventional approaches. Interrater reliability (Gwet's AC1) was evaluated for hybrid and conventional interpretation. Interrater reliability was significantly higher for hybrid than conventional approach (AC1 = .81, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .73-.89 vs. AC1 = .43, 95% CI = .32-.53; p < .001). Review time was markedly reduced (median [interquartile range (IQR)] = 2.2 [.5-4.3] vs. 52.4 [33.2-62.9] min, mean [95% CI] = 2.9 [2.5-3.2] vs. 50.8 [46.5-55.2] min, p < .001), a 95.8% median reduction (IQR = 95.6-96.3). Diagnostic performance comparisons were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm-Bonferroni procedure across all 63 tests. The hybrid approach showed significantly higher sensitivity than conventional interpretation (.88, 95% CI = .77-.97 vs. .69, 95% CI = .57-.81; adjusted p = .006). Its numerically higher diagnostic accuracy versus conventional interpretation (.75, 95% CI = .66-.83 vs. .68, 95% CI = .61-.74) was nonsignificant after correction (adjusted p > .99). Hybrid approach diagnostic accuracy was significantly greater than fully automated analysis (.75, 95% CI = .66-.83 vs. .55, 95% CI = .44-.65; adjusted p < .001). Expert oversight of AI-assisted categorization of interictal epileptiform and nonepileptiform EEG abnormalities improves interrater reliability and efficiency, increases diagnostic sensitivity versus conventional interpretation, and increases diagnostic accuracy versus fully automated analysis in adult LTM.

ai.reason: AI seizure-abnormality classification in long-term EEG has some transferable classification relevance, but it is a clinical validation study rather than a lightweight or generalizable method contribution.
ai.summary: Evaluated the clinically approved autoSCORE AI for long-term EEG monitoring interpretation, showing that a hybrid AI-expert approach achieved higher interrater reliability (AC1=0.81 vs. 0.43) and reduced review time by 95.8% compared to conventional analysis, with improved sensitivity (0.88 vs. 0.69). Diagnostic accuracy of the hybrid approach was higher than fully automated analysis.

papers.title: An explainable machine learning model based on multidimensional task-state electroencephalography for identifying attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder comorbid developmental dyslexia.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and developmental dyslexia (DD) are highly comorbid, yet objective differentiation from individual disorders remains challenging due to the lack of neurophysiological biomarkers. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model leveraging multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD-DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development (TD). Ninety children (27 ADHD-DD, 40 ADHD, 23 TD) underwent EEG during a VSWM task. Five feature categories were extracted: event-related potentials, time-frequency characteristics, functional connectivity, graph-theoretic metrics, and nonlinear dynamics. Three feature-processing strategies and nine classifiers were compared within a nested cross-validation framework. Feature contribution was quantified by coefficient back-projection of the optimal PCA-LR mode. Sensitivity and permutation analyses were performed. The PCA-LR model achieved a balanced accuracy of 80.5%, a Macro-F1 of 0.799, and a Macro-AUC of 0.912. Class-wise AUCs were 0.905 for ADHD-DD, 0.904 for ADHD, and 0.927 for TD. Left temporal α-band functional connectivity was a shared high-contribution feature in both disorder groups. ADHD-DD was distinguished by widely distributed cross-regional connectivity spanning θ and α bands and by P200 amplitude. ADHD was characterized primarily by α-band network metrics and α-ERD, whereas TD relied mainly on θ and α bands functional connectivity and graph-theoretic metrics. Our findings suggest that multidimensional task-state EEG features may help differentiate children with ADHD-DD comorbidity from those with ADHD or typical development. They also indicate that machine-learning approaches may be useful for identifying neurodevelopmental comorbid conditions.

ai.summary: Developed an explainable PCA-LR model using multidimensional task-state EEG features to distinguish ADHD-DD comorbidity from ADHD and typical development, achieving balanced accuracy of 80.5% and Macro-AUC of 0.912. Left temporal alpha-band functional connectivity was a shared high-contribution feature across disorder groups.

papers.title: Frequency extraction from invariant flows.
papers.abstract: In nondegenerate integrable Hamiltonian systems, invariant tori can be parametrized by action variables or fundamental frequencies. We introduce an invariant-flow formulation, consistent with the Liouville-Arnold geometry, for extracting these frequencies. Treating invariants as generators of commuting Hamiltonian flows yields the frequencies from time-of-flight parameters, providing a direct alternative to action-angle constructions and long-time spectral analysis. The resulting numerical procedure extends naturally to multiple degrees of freedom and achieves high accuracy for the McMillan map. More broadly, the framework provides an invariant-centered view of near-integrable dynamics, recovering frequencies and other dynamical information from high-quality approximate invariants.

papers.title: Aging Is Associated with Reduced Topographic Differentiation Between Speaking and Silent Reading
papers.abstract: Aging affects how neural activity is organized and specialized, but its impact on neural differentiation across language tasks remains unclear. In this study, we investigated whether aging influences neural differentiation during speaking and silent reading. Fifteen young adults and 15 older adults completed speaking and silent-reading tasks in a delayed-response paradigm while we collected electroencephalography (EEG) data. We examined EEG signal strength using time-resolved global field power (GFP), spatial configuration using topographic analysis of variance (TANOVA), and task-specific neural differentiation using the global dissimilarity index (DISS). We also examined the relationship between neural and behavioral measures, including digit-span scores and speech onset time. We found that speaking was associated with higher GFP than silent reading in the 388-800 ms interval, with no significant effects of group or group x task interaction, indicating similar EEG strength across groups. TANOVA revealed age-related differences in scalp topography in the 229-334 ms and 377-538 ms intervals, a task effect in the 618-723 ms interval, and a group x task interaction in the 562-636 ms interval. Notably, young adults had greater DISS than older adults during the 508-629 ms and 660-800 ms intervals, reflecting more distinct neural configurations for speaking and reading. We did not find significant correlations between DISS or GFP and behavioral measures, and the two groups performed similarly on behavioral measures. Overall, aging was associated with reduced neural differentiation between speaking and silent reading, especially during later processing stages (e.g., motor command preparation), while preserving overall EEG activity and behavioral performance. These findings may suggest that aging reduces neural network specificity (as previously suggested) and alters spatial organization without necessarily impairing behavior.

ai.reason: Topographic ANOVA and global dissimilarity measures are transferable spatial EEG techniques, though the aging language-task application is adjacent to core interests.
ai.summary: Investigated aging effects on neural differentiation during speaking and silent reading using EEG in young and older adults, finding reduced global dissimilarity between tasks in older adults during later processing stages (508-629 ms and 660-800 ms) despite similar overall EEG strength and behavioral performance.

papers.title: Dorsolateral prefrontal TMS-evoked N100 as a neurophysiological correlate of symptom change in adolescent depression.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly prevalent in adolescence. Up to 30% of patients insufficiently benefit from first-line treatments, underscoring the need for improved treatment strategies and better understanding of pathophysiology. In depression, an imbalance between cortical excitation and inhibition in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), assessed by the TMS-evoked N100 potential, is suggested as one of several contributing neurobiological mechanisms. While elevated N100 amplitudes have been observed in depressed adults and adolescents, its association with symptom change remains insufficiently investigated. In a randomized controlled trial, N = 54 adolescents (38 girls, 16 boys) with MDD received six weeks of whole body vibration training (exercising on a vibrating plate that triggers involuntary muscle contractions through a neurological reflex) or light stretching as add-on treatments to treatment as usual. TMS-EEG was applied before and after the intervention to assess N100 amplitudes over the left and right DLPFC. Depressive symptoms were measured using the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised. Changes in N100 amplitudes were analyzed using repeated measures ANOVA. Multiple regression analyses with intervention group as predictor examined associations between changes in N100 amplitudes and depressive symptoms, including sex as moderator and a subsequent girls-only analysis. Across both groups, N100 amplitudes significantly decreased from pre-to post-intervention. No differential effects between interventions were observed. Reductions in right-hemispheric N100 amplitudes were significantly associated with improvements in depressive symptoms. This association reached statistical significance in girls. Our findings support the N100 as a candidate neurophysiological correlate of depressive symptom improvement.

A cornerstone of these interactions is rhythm categorisation, allowing the sheer diversity of rhythmic inputs to be mapped onto internal rhythm categories. However, this view appears to conflict with the diversity of music practices across cultures, which points to a role of experience in rhythm categorisation. To assess the relative contributions of neurobiological predispositions and experience, we tested 0- to 3-day-old newborns, capitalising on their minimal postnatal experience with music. Using electroencephalography (EEG), we recorded, in newborns and adults, brain responses to drum sounds whose pattern of relative interval duration ranged from isochronous to long-short rhythms (1:1 - 2:1 interval ratio). Results indicate significant categorisation in newborns's neural responses, with a representational structure that correlate with those of adults, yet with a greater degree of differentiation across rhythms. papers.title: Decoding morality through EEG with ML: rigour, risks, and the road ahead.
papers.abstract: The quest to decode morality through electroencephalography (EEG) with machine learning (ML) is as much about confronting the risks of opaque algorithms as it is about harnessing their scientific promise. This systematic review synthesises 17 empirical studies published between 2018 and 2025 that employed ML or deep learning (DL) approaches to EEG data within moral cognition paradigms. Following PRISMA guidelines, studies were identified across four electronic databases and categorised into eight experimental paradigms spanning three thematic branches: Evaluation, Emotion, and Prosociality. The Ultimatum Game was the most frequently applied paradigm (n = 6), while classical ML approaches dominated methodological choices, accounting for 65% of the included studies. Despite the growing interest in DL, interpretability was inconsistently addressed, with Explainable Artificial Intelligence methods applied in only one of the six DL studies and in just two of the 17 included studies overall. This review highlights three pressing methodological gaps: the need for multimodal fusion to capture richer neural signals, the integration of transfer learning to enhance generalisability, and the adoption of standardised interpretability reporting to ensure transparency. We argue that ML offers a scientifically rigorous pathway for advancing EEG-based moral cognition research, but only when models are robustly validated and their outputs rendered explainable. Without these safeguards, the promise of decoding morality risks being undermined by opaque algorithms and methodological blind spots. papers.title: Comparative assessment of AD8232- and MAX30003-based ECG acquisition paths using synthetic ECG signals.
papers.abstract: This study presents a comparative technical evaluation of two implemented electrocardiogram (ECG) acquisition paths based on AD8232 and MAX30003 under controlled laboratory conditions. Signal similarity after preprocessing was assessed using time-domain metrics, including Pearson correlation, mean absolute error, root mean square error (RMSE), and normalized RMSE. In addition, spectral analysis based on Welch's method was performed using absolute bandpower values and relative bandpower indices. Error metrics remained low and comparable between recordings. Relative spectral indices showed implementation-specific differences between the complete acquisition paths, particularly in the 50 Hz component band, whereas the 40-60 Hz band was retained only as an auxiliary descriptive upper-band index because of the different filtering and digitization architectures of the two paths. EC significantly increased high-frequency global coherence in all five of the participants, yet it did not consistently affect Lempel-Ziv complexity or power across participants. papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.abstract: How do leader and follower roles shape the brain mechanisms that support coordinated action between people? This question has therapeutic relevance for conditions such as schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder, where the capacity for reciprocal social coordination is a defining vulnerability. Here, we propose a tetradic framework and examine sensorimotor coordination in 16 healthy adult pairs (15 included in EEG analyses) using dual-brain EEG hyperscanning and a 2x2 within-subject design crossing Role (Leader/Follower) and Condition (Mirroring/Matching). Mirroring required resonance with a partner's movement; Matching required its controlled transformation. This contrast was designed to dissociate automatic from controlled coordination. Behaviourally, Mirroring produced a robust Follower reaction-time advantage: pooling an independent behavioural-only cohort (combined N=64) revealed a smaller Leader advantage, consistent with role-dependent attention-inhibition gating. At the neural level, tonic power and significant phasic condition clusters were greater during Matching than Mirroring, while role-dependent phasic clusters suggested an anticipatory sequence around Leader responses and post-response gating and rebound around Follower responses. Information-theoretic decomposition identified Leader-weighted predictive information in frontal and posterior perceptual regions, Follower-specific adaptive information across frontoparietal and sensorimotor cortices, sparse Synergy in lateral occipital, fusiform, and paracentral cortices, and Redundancy linking pars opercularis and lateral occipital cortex. These findings characterize tetradic coordination within dyads as a multiscale, role-asymmetric architecture in which top-down predictive control and bottom-up adaptive regulation are functionally dissociable. The baseline simulation used r = 0.20000 day-1, α = 0.05000 day-1, β = 0.35000 day-1, γ = 0.30000 day-1, T0 = 0.50000, and N0 = 0.40000. Explicit Euler integration was performed with Δt = 0.01 day over 20 days. A descriptive nonlinear regression fit, Fourier spectral analysis, 1-parameter sensitivity analyses, and joint α-β sensitivity analysis were applied to the simulated trajectory. papers.title: Seizures Secondary to Aconitum Plant Poisoning: a case report.
papers.abstract: Aconitum plant poisoning typically manifests as isolated early cardiotoxicity or late neurotoxicity. However, the dynamic temporal evolution from arrhythmia-driven cardiogenic syncope to true epileptic seizures mediated by direct central nervous system injury remains rarely documented and poorly characterized. We report a 53-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with ventricular tachycardia rapidly degenerating into ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest following ingestion of homemade Aconitum kusnezoffii (caowu)-infused liquor. Initial convulsions were tightly coupled with malignant arrhythmias, consistent with cardiogenic syncope. After successful resuscitation, hemoperfusion, and restoration of stable sinus rhythm, the patient developed breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizures on hospital days 4-6. Electroencephalography performed during sedation withdrawal revealed bilateral occipital spike-and-slow and sharp-and-slow waves with focal epileptiform discharges, confirming direct central nervous system neurotoxicity rather than recurrent cardiac ischemia. A mechanism-based, staged treatment strategy was employed: early advanced cardiac life support and hemoperfusion targeted cardiotoxicity, while sodium valproate and acetylglutamine were administered for antiepileptic prophylaxis and neuroprotection. The patient was discharged on day 13; antiepileptic therapy was successfully tapered and discontinued at 3 months without seizure recurrence, with normalization of electroencephalography and electrocardiography. This case provides the first systematic documentation, validated by electroencephalography, of the transition from cardiogenic convulsions to true epileptic seizures in Aconitum alkaloid poisoning. The findings highlight the critical role of pharmacokinetic-driven central nervous system retention in delayed seizure onset and underscore the necessity of prolonged neurological monitoring, early electroencephalography evaluation for late-onset convulsions, and sustained antiepileptic prophylaxis to reduce mortality and long-term neurological sequelae. Aconitum plant poisoning may manifest as early cardiogenic syncope and convulsions secondary to malignant arrhythmias, progressing in the late stage to genuine seizures caused by central nervous system (CNS) injury. Effective management requires a staged treatment strategy targeting both cardiotoxicity and neurotoxicity, with a focus on stabilizing cardiac rhythm and providing neuroprotection as needed.

papers.title: Copenhagen Magnetic Personalized Accelerated Brain Circuit Therapy (CoMPACT) trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blinded, sham-controlled, three-armed, parallel-group trial of transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment-resistant depression.
papers.abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD), characterized by poor response to conventional antidepressant therapies, remains a major clinical challenge. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) has emerged as a promising alternative. Employing intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS), TMS protocols have yielded rapid antidepressant effects in recent accelerated treatment studies. These findings warrant further investigation in larger samples to confirm efficacy and in-depth investigation into the underlying mechanisms. Moreover, other cortical sites may also represent suitable targets for accelerated iTBS treatment of TRD. This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will assess the efficacy, feasibility and mechanisms of a novel, personalized, and accelerated iTBS protocol for TRD, targeting two left hemispheric regions, the left dlPFC and inferior parietal lobule (IPL), both characterized by anticorrelated functional connectivity with the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex. 78 adults (aged 18-95 years) will be recruited from Danish mental health centers and randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) active iTBS of the left dlPFC, (2) active iTBS targeting of the left IPL, or (3) sham iTBS at either site. The intervention includes five daily sessions over five consecutive days. Targeting informed by group-level functional connectivity will be combined with individualized coil placement and stimulation dosing using electric field modeling based on whole-brain anatomical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Antidepressant efficacy will be evaluated using the 6-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale as the primary outcome, assessed at an early post-intervention follow-up (F1) within three days after the final stimulation session. Multimodal post-treatment assessments, including MRI, will be conducted within five days after the intervention (T1). A four-week follow-up (T2) will assess the durability of clinical and cognitive outcomes. Neurophysiological mechanisms will be investigated using electroencephalography as well as structural and functional MRI. By testing a novel stimulation protocol and evaluating the efficacy of a new parietal target, this study will help advance the development of innovative, circuit-based interventions for TRD, with potential implications for broader applications across neuropsychiatry. https://clinicaltrials.gov/, identifier NCT06895863.

papers.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
papers.abstract: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light-gated K+ channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single-cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro-arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na+ (by 15.1% vs. 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na+ permeability of currently available K+-conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re-entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm2. Complementary tissue-scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na+ channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large-conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Re-entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high-voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light-gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light-gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non-selective cation- and anion-conducting channels terminate re-entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro-arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K+-conducting channels largely avoid this pro-arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na+ accumulation attributable to residual Na+ permeability. Together, these trade-offs define clear clinical implications: K+-conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K+ selectivity and red-shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood-perfused myocardium become available. KEY POINTS: We use computational simulations to compare cation non-selective (ChR2), anion non-selective (GtACR1) and K+-selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re-entrant arrhythmia. Single-cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca2+, which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re-entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue-scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na+ channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large-conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

papers.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Recreational nitrous oxide (N2O) inhalation is increasingly prevalent among young adults, but acute psychiatric presentations following short-term binge exposure remain poorly characterized. We report a case of a female in her early 20s with no prior history of psychotic illness who developed an acute psychotic and dissociative syndrome over three days at an outdoor music festival. Her presentation followed heavy recreational N2O and 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) exposure combined with sleep deprivation. On admission, she exhibited profound disorientation, inability to recognize close family members, polymorphic delusions, passivity phenomena, and auditory and olfactory hallucinations, requiring involuntary psychiatric hospitalization. Diagnostic workup revealed normal brain and cervical spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and a normal electroencephalogram (EEG) without epileptiform activity or slowing. Serum homocysteine was moderately elevated (25.2 µmol/L) alongside a low-normal vitamin B12 concentration (270 pg/mL), consistent with N2O-induced functional cobalamin deficiency; both markers normalized following parenteral vitamin B12 and oral folic acid supplementation. During inpatient stay, treatment with risperidone was followed by progressive neutropenia, which fully resolved after cross-titration to aripiprazole. She gradually regained full insight, was discharged on day 12, and remained free of psychotic symptoms at her three-week outpatient review. This case suggests that short-term binge N2O exposure, together with MDMA and sleep deprivation, may contribute to severe neuropsychiatric presentations without chronic use; it illustrates the value of measuring homocysteine rather than relying solely on serum B12 levels; and highlights potential hematological adverse effects during antipsychotic initiation.

papers.title: Global trends and knowledge structure of cardiovascular magnetocardiography research: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading global health threat. Recent advances in room-temperature sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) have renewed research interest in the clinical translation of magnetocardiography (MCG) for cardiovascular diagnosis, yet the global research evolution of MCG has yet to be quantitatively characterized. Literature from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus (2000-2026) was analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and R to evaluate publication trends, knowledge networks, and evolving frontiers. A total of 631 WoSCC and 755 Scopus articles were included. The publication trajectory exhibits a prolonged plateau followed by substantial recent growth. Germany, the United States, and China are the most prolific contributors. Keyword analysis revealed a diversification of technological and analytical themes. While early literature was strongly associated with superconducting quantum interference devices-based MCG, recent research has increasingly highlighted optically pumped magnetometers, magnetic-field control, sensor arrays, magnetic noise suppression, and AI-based signal analysis. The application landscape has broadened from physiological validation to coronary artery disease diagnosis, arrhythmia assessment, and fetal electrophysiology. Collectively, these findings suggest that the evolution of cardiovascular MCG reflects the parallel development and interaction of sensor technologies, AI-based analysis, and emerging clinical applications. Future research should prioritize standardized protocols, scalable and robust acquisition systems, and explainable AI models to accelerate clinical implementation.

papers.title: Clinical features and outcomes of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis.
papers.abstract: To explore the clinical characteristics of atezolizumab-associated encephalitis and to provide clinical evidence for diagnosis and treatment. Clinical reports on atezolizumab-associated encephalitis published before June 30, 2026 were collected for retrospective analysis by searching Chinese and English databases. A total of 39 cases of encephalitis were included, with a median age of 60 years (33, 78). The median time of symptom onset was 14 days (2, 420) after the initial administration. Fever (53.8%), confusion (51.3%) and headache (28.2%) were the main complaints of the patients. Cerebrospinal fluid examination showed elevated white blood cell count and protein, with median values of 27 cells/μL (1, 553) and 133mg/dL (27.1, 815), respectively. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed T2 fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintensities in half of the patients. Electroencephalogram showed display epileptiform discharges (26.7%) and slow waves (40.0%). After discontinuation of atezolizumab and initiation of targeted treatment, 97.4% of patients achieved symptomatic improvement or recovery, while 2.6% died of encephalitis-related complications. Patients with atezolizumab-associated encephalitis were predominantly middle-aged and elderly, with fever, confusion and headache as the major manifestations. Clinicians should be alert to the potential risk of encephalitis during atezolizumab treatment. Most patients obtained symptom relief or clinical recovery following atezolizumab discontinuation and treatment; only a few succumbed to severe encephalitis-related complications.

papers.title: Structural, dielectric behavior, diffuse phase transition, and electrical properties of 0.7(Bi1-x Sm x ) FeO3-0.3BaTiO3 ceramics (x = 0.1 and 0.2).
papers.abstract: Environmentally friendly 0.7(Bi1-x Sm x )FeO3-0.3BaTiO3 systems with various doping rates with x = 0.1 and 0.2, have been synthesized by the solid-state method, and their structural, microstructural, vibrational, and electrical properties were systematically investigated. X-ray diffraction combined with Rietveld refinement confirmed the stabilization of a single-phase perovskite structure, with lattice contraction attributed to Sm3+ substitution. The BFBT-0.1Sm composition crystallizes in a tetragonal phase with P4/mmm symmetry, whereas the BFBT-0.2Sm sample adopts an orthorhombic structure belonging to the Pmmm space group. This structural evolution is consistently supported by both XRD patterns and Raman spectral analysis. SEM analysis revealed dense microstructures with well-distributed grains. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) confirmed the presence of all the chemical elements constituting the materials. Raman spectroscopy provided evidence of local structural distortion. Dielectric measurements showed a significant increase in permittivity, while impedance and AC conductivity analyses indicated a thermally activated hopping mechanism consistent with Jonscher's power law. The dielectric constant varies with temperature, indicating the occurrence of a diffuse phase transition. This behavior was further analyzed using the modified Curie-Weiss law. A thorough analysis of the dielectric properties as a function of temperature demonstrates a characteristic ferroelectric to paraelectric (FE-PE) transition, marked by a significant rise in the real part of permittivity near 600-700 K for both compounds. This substantial permittivity underscores their potential for energy storage applications. These findings suggest that the studied ceramics are promising candidates for multifunctional devices.

papers.title: Adsorptive Removal of 1,2-Dichloroethane Using Novel Oleogel Adsorbents: Synthesis Strategy and Adsorption Mechanism Insight.
papers.abstract: 1,2-Dichloroethane (DCE) is a widely used, highly volatile, and lipophilic industrial solvent. As a chlorine-containing volatile organic compound (VOC), DCE emissions pose significant risks to human health and the ecological environment. Adsorption is considered an economical and environmentally friendly method for eliminating air pollutants. In this study, novel Oleogel adsorbents were prepared via self-assembly and polymeric cross-linking mechanisms, using 12-hydroxystearic acid (12-HSA) and ethyl cellulose (EC) as gelators, and rapeseed oil (RO) and dioctyl adipate (DOA) as base oils. A series of oleogels were fabricated by varying the type and dosage of gelators, and their structures, physicochemical properties, and DCE adsorption performance were systematically characterized. The DCE adsorption behavior and mechanism were investigated through dynamic adsorption experiments, multimodel kinetic fitting, and spectral analysis at multiple temperatures. The results showed that the 10 wt % 12-HSA/DOA Oleogel achieved a DCE adsorption capacity of 154.4 mg g-1 at 25 °C and reached 201.9 mg g-1 at 15 °C, which is comparable to those of previously reported adsorbents. Characterization and adsorption experiments demonstrated that the adsorbent exhibited a stable three-dimensional crystalline architecture, excellent oil retention (up to 98% after centrifugation), and favorable thermal stability below 150 °C. Meanwhile, DCE adsorption on Oleogel adsorbents involves significant intermolecular interactions (e.g., dipole-dipole and hydrogen bonding) rather than a purely physical process, and their surface is enriched with exposed functional groups, such as carbonyl and carboxyl groups. Further analysis indicated that the base oil was the dominant factor governing DCE adsorption performance, and the gelator type was the decisive factor influencing crystal morphology development. Notably, the contact angle of samples prepared from ethyl cellulose and dioctyl adipate reached 95.6°, suggesting potential for use in high-humidity environments.
